blocks.x: Chain-of-custody evidence is becoming a market-access requirement, not a marketing story.
EUDR made provenance a compliance deadline. Capture at source (mobile-first for farmers) decides data quality more than ledger choice.
Role-based verification: regulators, buyers and auditors each see only what their role permits.
Verified provenance is premium positioning — the market pays for proof.
Where it breaks in practice: technology-first scoping: a chain chosen before the trust question is answered, producing a ledger everyone must trust but nobody needs.

The strongest counter-case, stated fairly: the trust-first thesis can end in a ledger nobody joins. Shared truth only pays when every participant's incentives point the same way — verify that before the protocol choice.
The practice, as we run it

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: we put the record on rails — immutable event history, selective disclosure, and integrations your counterparties' auditors accept. Every program in the Blockchain & Digital Trust domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
